title: Jumper's Knee

positions.as_written: Take the history: pain at the front of the knee that comes on with jumping or landing, worse at the start of activity, and worse after rather than during in the early stages.
Repeat with the knee flexed and the tendon tensioned, where the tenderness typically reduces.
Ask the patient to perform a single leg decline squat or a single leg squat, and note whether it reproduces the pain.
Assess the quadriceps and the proximal control, since both contribute to the load the tendon carries.
